tools.name: show_pets
tools.description: Show adoptable pets near a place as an interactive view: photos, facts, and a button to meet one at its rescue. Use it when someone wants to look at pets to adopt. Apps without interactive views get the same list as text.

tools.name: find_pets
tools.description: Search adoptable pets at rescues and shelters (and, in some cities, found pets: marked found:true, announced for their owners first, not adoptable yet; pass found=exclude to leave them out): near a US ZIP, lat,lon or a Taiwan county or township in any language (near, with miles or km; sorted by dist

tools.name: resolve_place
tools.description: Turn a US ZIP, lat,lon or a Taiwan county or township name (any language) into the point and radius find_pets would search around, to confirm with the person before searching. Positions are rounded to about 1 km and nothing is stored.

tools.name: resolve_breed
tools.description: Turn a breed name in any language (貴賓犬, pit bull, perro salchicha, 시바견) into Wikidata breed ids, to pass to find_pets as breed or to compare listings across countries.

tools.name: get_pet
tools.description: One adoptable pet by id (from find_pets): photos, temperament, good-with, adoption fee, the rescue and how to reach it.

tools.name: get_rescue
tools.description: One rescue or shelter by id (from a pet's rescue.id): where it is, its adoption page, email and phone.

tools.name: search_by_description
tools.description: Find pets to adopt from a sentence in any language (found pets, marked found:true, are not adoptable yet): “a calm small dog that is good with kids, under 10 kg, near Springfield”. Returns the pets AND what was understood (understood.chips: species, breed, age, size, good-with, place, radius...), so

tools.name: similar_pets
tools.description: Pets similar to one pet id (from search results): same kind of pet and size, nearest in meaning of their listings. Use it after the person likes one pet.

tools.name: about_this_service
tools.description: Where the listings come from, who runs this service, what it keeps, and how a rescue changes or removes its listings.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_rescue · Public sink: get_rescue · Destructive: search_by_description.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_rescue · Public sink: get_rescue · Destructive: search_by_description

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
